approach: Add a pending-introspection queue as JSON files under the state directory (`<state>/introspect-pending/`), following the `steward-pending` precedent (steward.rs:1163). `introspect_job` and `introspect_intervention` build the event as today, then call a new `run_or_defer(event, ui)`. It checks `self.state.registry().stopped()` before `introspect` can reach `driver.invoke` (introspect.rs:1433). When the switch is on it writes one file per event and returns None; otherwise it runs `introspect`, which is unchanged, so a model failure is still a failed record. A new `Athena::start_with(ui)` turns the switch off and then drains. `Athena::start()` (manage.rs:504) keeps `Result<bool>` and calls `start_with(&Quiet)`, so `the_kill_switch_blocks_new_work` (lifecycle.rs:1719) compiles unchanged. The drain first queues each kill-switch failure by rule (a failed introspection whose `failure` contains `the kill switch is on`, with no other introspection for the same job or intervention and not already pending). That reaches the two named jobs without editing records/. It then runs each pending event through `introspect`, oldest first, and deletes the file once the record is committed. The CLI `start()` in commands.rs calls `start_with`. No record, status, schema, athena.toml or gate change. Revision: the demonstration for criterion 7 now sets `fails_without` and `seam`. The rest of the plan is as accepted in round 1.

decisions.choice: Queue deferred events as files in the state directory, not as a new record status or record type.
decisions.reason: The brief forbids a new status or schema change. State-directory files leave `AnyRecord`, `check_record_file`, the records allow-list and the round-trip test untouched. `steward-pending` (steward.rs:1163-1196) is the same pattern. Pending is local machine state and needs no history.

decisions.choice: Check `stopped()` in a new `run_or_defer` called by `introspect_job` and `introspect_intervention`; `introspect` is unchanged and is also what the drain calls.
decisions.reason: One check before the model is reachable. Both entry points and their three callers (run/mod.rs:421, reading.rs:1374, manage.rs:400) get the deferral with no per-caller edit. The drain calls `introspect` and is not re-deferred.

decisions.choice: Requeue old failures by rule (failed record, failure text contains `the kill switch is on`, no other introspection for the same job or intervention), not by a hard-coded id list.

Add a private `event_key(&Event) -> String` (`job-<id>` for Rejection/Failure triggers, `intervention-<id>` otherwise), `defer(&self, event, ui) -> Result<()>` (create the directory, write `<key>.json`, skip if it exists, print a line saying the introspection is deferred until `athena start`), and `pub fn pending_introspections(&self) -> Vec<Event>` (read the directory, ignore unreadable files, sort by file name).

In introspect.rs add `fn run_or_defer(&self, event, ui) -> Result<Option<IntrospectionRecord>>`: if `self.state.registry().stopped()`, call `defer` and return `Ok(None)`; otherwise `self.introspect(event, ui).map(Some)`. Change `introspect_job` (1273-1276) and `introspect_intervention` (1286-1288) to call it. Leave `introspect` unchanged.

In introspect.rs add `requeue_kill_switch_failures(&self) -> Result<usize>`: load `GitRecords` at `self.head()?`; for each introspection with status Failed and `failure` containing `the kill switch is on`, compute its event key from `trigger`, `job` and `intervention`; skip it when any other introspection has the same key or the key is pending; rebuild the event with `event_of_job` or `event_of_intervention` (skip on None or Err) and `defer` it quietly. Add `pub fn run_pending_introspections(&self, ui) -> usize`: return 0 when `self.nested.is_some()`; call the requeue scan (errors become ui lines); then for each pending file, stop if `stopped()`, call `introspect`, delete the file on Ok, print the error and keep the file on Err. Return the number run. In manage.rs change `start` to `self.start_with(&crate::Quiet)` and add `pub fn start_with(&self, ui: &dyn Ui) -> Result<bool>`: `let was = self.state.registry().start()?; self.run_pending_introspections(ui); Ok(was)`.

For the requeue test, seed a failed `IntrospectionRecord` (built as the existing record literal near line 1091 does) with failure `the model could not run: the kill switch is on (`athena start` turns it off)` for a rejected chain job, and a second with failure `model unavailable` for another job. Assert that `start` reruns only the first (one new Recorded record, `model.prompts` length 1) and that a second `start` adds none.

Add the CHANGELOG.md bullet under Unreleased / Added and append decision D177 to docs/decisions.md (next free number), with Case, Decision, Alternatives, Tradeoff, Reversal cost and a Provenance bullet naming the files read and the tests run.

Run `cargo fmt --all`, then `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked`, and fix anything they report. Do not touch records/, athena.toml, defaults.toml or workflows. After the change lands, the owner runs `athena start` once; the requeue scan then finds the failed introspections of jobs 20261029-142858-5c0p and 20261017-155259-7mjc and reruns them with the real model. That step needs a Claude model and cannot be run by the producer.

risks.risk: The requeue rule matches more failed records than the two named, so one `athena start` could spend several model calls.
risks.mitigation: The rule needs the exact phrase 'the kill switch is on' and no other introspection for the event. Each rerun adds a record, so an event is rerun at most once. The CHANGELOG entry and D177 state the cost.

risks.risk: Two `athena start` processes drain at the same moment and run the same pending event twice.
risks.mitigation: Unlikely for a manual command; the drain deletes each file after the commit, so a later start finds none, and the requeue rule excludes an event that already has a second introspection. Not claimed race-free; D177 notes it.

risks.risk: The drain runs on every `athena start` and adds a records load to a command that did not read records before; a repository without commits or with an unreadable head would fail it.
risks.mitigation: Drain errors become ui lines and never fail `start`. The scan runs only when `self.head()` succeeds, and the drain returns early when nothing is pending and the scan finds nothing.

risks.risk: If `introspect` returns Err (a commit failure), the file stays and is retried on every start.
risks.mitigation: The error is shown as a ui line each time. Only a commit failure leaves a file; a model failure commits a failed record, deletes the file and is not requeued.

risks.risk: The switch is turned on again during the drain.
risks.mitigation: The drain checks `stopped()` before each event and stops, leaving the rest pending. A switch set between the check and the model call gives a failed record with the kill-switch text, which the next start requeues by the same rule.

risks.risk: D177 may collide with a decision number added by another job.
risks.mitigation: The producer takes the next free number after the last `## D` heading in docs/decisions.md when it appends.

risks.risk: The criterion 7 checks fail late because of formatting or an unused helper.
risks.mitigation: The producer runs `cargo fmt --all` and the clippy and test commands before finishing, and keeps every new helper used by `run_or_defer` or the drain.
